title: Esna to Aswan: the dahabiya route
standfirst: Dahabiyas usually sail between Esna and Aswan over four or five nights, mooring at quiet banks and stopping at sites the big ships pass by. For other routes, see [[up]].

sections.heading: Why dahabiyas start at Esna
paragraphs: Starting south of the Esna lock avoids the queue of ships waiting to pass it, and the stretch from Esna to Aswan has the quiet moorings and smaller sites that suit a sailing boat.

sections.heading: What you see
paragraphs: Edfu and Kom Ombo, like the ships, and smaller places such as El Kab and the sandstone quarries of Gebel Silsila. Luxor is usually visited before boarding, by road from Esna.

sections.heading: Good to know
paragraphs: Days follow the wind, and a tug tows the dahabiya when it drops, so stops and times are kept. Evenings are spent at riverbanks and islands, away from other boats.

faqs.q: Is Luxor included on a dahabiya cruise?
faqs.a: Usually not as part of the sailing. Many travellers spend a day or two in Luxor before transferring to Esna.

faqs.q: How long is the dahabiya route?
faqs.a: Four or five nights between Esna and Aswan.

seoDescription: The dahabiya route from Esna to Aswan: why it starts at Esna, the quiet stops, and how the days run.
